mechaber/1:main: THE LAWS OF LEAVING WATER OVERNIGHT One may not knead except with water that was left overnight, whether they are waters of a pool or of a spring or whether they are waters of a river and they should be drawn while it is still day (close to the twilight period) or during the twilight period. One should not knead with them until the entire night has passed. One is able to draw large quantities of water in a single day. If it is hot at the time [of drawing], they[the waters] should be placed in the wine cellar which is cooler and if it is cold at the time, they should be placed out in the open, for the wine cellar is warmer, and one must rise early and bring them into the house prior to the sun rising, even if it's a cloudy day. REMA: and [regarding] if they were not brought in early, if they didn't stand [outside] to the extent that they became warm, they are not tainted. Ideally, the water should be left standing under the ceiling in case one forgets to bring them in early . When transporting the water under the open sky, one should cover it . When Pesach occurs on the first of the week, one should draw the waters on the outset of the 13th which is [solar] Thursday night . Initially, one should draw from the rivers and not from the wells . However, when the rivers are expanded from the thawing snow and rainfall, ideally one should draw from the wells . One should not spill water left overnight because of a death or the falling of a period [tekoopha] . Nevertheless, initially, its good to place iron in them [the water containers]. Also, it is forbidden for a gentile to draw the water for Mitzvah Matzos and even regarding other Matzot, a Jew should draw the water if possible. It is customary to gather water specifically for the Matzah[s] of the Mitzvah and to take [the water in] new earthenware vessels and one should not deviate from the custom. Regarding a wooden vessel, one need not be strict (about all this) {Rama: (His own words and Haghot Maimoni perek 5) (B"Y in the name of A"CH) (T"H siman 115 in the name of SMA"G and SMA"K and MA"HA"RIK) (Mordechai end of the first perek of Pesachim) (ASHR"Y and Mordechai} (MAHA"RIV} (Mordechai perek "kol sha'ah" and Haghaot Maimony perek 5} (Mordechai and MAHA"RI on RI"N and MAHA"RIL)}
mechaber/2:main: There are those who say regarding water which was brought into a "Soostirnah" that it is permitted to knead with them around the time they were drawn and one shouldn't be lenient regarding this if the situation does not require it.
mechaber/3:main: One should not knead in hot water even if it was only warmed by the sun and not with water which was gathered from a large boil tank of thick copper which is suspended over a fire-place and the water within is thawed even if there is no fire underneath. If one transgressed [this] and kneaded [whether] with these waters, or waters which were not left overnight, it is forbidden. There are those who dispute this and permit kneading with water which was not left overnight and there are those who say that when used accidentally, it is permitted and where the situation requires it, one may rely on these [opinions]. REMA: and even in when not required, if one accidentally transgressed and kneaded with water which was not left overnight, one is permitted to use it. {Rama: (Rabbe Yeruchem and B"Y)}
mechaber/4:main: [Regarding] water which was not left overnight that became dissolved, at a ratio of 1:2, in water which was left overnight, one may knead with these.
mechaber/5:main: It is customary to not place salt in the Matzah and this is the proper thing and even subsequently one should forbid it {Rama: (Mordechai and also his own words)}
mechaber/6:main: [Regarding] kneading with caraway, sesame and other types of seasonings, it's kosher [for the Mitzvah] since there is the taste of Matzah. Nevertheless, one shouldn't place in seasonings, as they are focused [spicy] and will heat the dough REMA: and if pepper [was added], even subsequently it is forbidden and similarly, if Lime Plaster fell in . {Rama: (MAHA"RIBv)}
baer-heitev/1:א: Close to bein ha shemashot. By right one should draw them at bein ha shemashot itself; and since not everyone knows how to measure bein ha shemashot, therefore one draws them close to bein ha shemashot after sunset (before moonrise). B'dieved, if one drew them while it was still day or drew after the beginning of the night, it appears from the words of the later authorities that one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours; and in responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than to draw early. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay — see Ateret Zekenim; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham. Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ב: Not harmful. And even if they stood in the sun. Beit Yosef and Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/1:ג: To cover them. Specifically an earthenware or wood vessel and the like — covering helps; but if they are in a glass vessel, covering does not help. Kaf HaChayim — see there.
baer-heitev/1:ד: On the night of the 5th. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor on Friday evening when they need to draw at bein ha shemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov (and if not for preparation it would certainly be permitted, for all shevut is permitted at bein ha shemashot) — therefore they draw on the night of the 5th that belongs to the 6th day, Beit Yosef; if so, also those who bake on the second day of Yom Tov are forbidden to draw at bein ha shemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need to draw on the eve of the 14th. It appears to me that if he forgot to draw on the night of the 5th he may draw on Friday while it is still day on this Erev Pesach. Or he may command a gentile to draw at bein ha shemashot — see siman 307. Or he may take water drawn in his house even though not drawn for the sake of the mitzvah, since it is impossible otherwise. Magen Avraham; see Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/1:ה: Iron. One takes new or clean iron and hangs it on a cord in the water, but one does not put his hand in the water, for the hand heats the water. In the rest of the year one places salt or a seal. Darkei Moshe, Magen Avraham. Taz wrote: it appears to me that on other nights, if one did not place iron in them to guard from the tekufah, one may pour them out if one can easily be without that water — which is not so with these waters of matzah of the mitzvah: it is forbidden to pour out, for it appears contemptuous of the verse "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil" — see there; and Kaf HaChayim practice filtering water — Maharil. Mateh Moshe wrote one should not take a vessel to draw water that had honey or fruit juice in it, for fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz as siman 462. (And likewise one should not take a copper vessel — Magen Avraham — and I have not seen practice so.) It appears to me that through boiling it is permitted. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/1:ז: Designated. One should say at the time of drawing for the sake of matzah of the mitzvah — Maharil and Mahariv; and Maharil wrote further that some are accustomed to take designated water each night independently.
baer-heitev/2:א: In a cistern (susternah). This is what they call in Talmudic language a pit — water collected in a building in the ground where the building separates it from the ground and it is also covered above, so it is as if they are drawn; one should not compare this to what we call in foreign language ar'ar kastin, for although it is covered above, one may not draw from it to use close to drawing because every hour and moment flows into it from the river. However, if one wishes to leave them overnight like other water and draw at its time, it is permitted to draw under the pipe or what they call in foreign language ar'ar, like from a river or a well drawn from it; and likewise from the kastin itself if it is covered. Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/2:ב: Pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even though there is concern they were drawn by day or at night — Kaf HaChayim, Ateret Zekenim. And in Halakhot Ketanot part 1 siman 97 he is lenient regarding rainwater collected from the air at night.
baer-heitev/3:א: Its copper rim. Rashi explained the rim is thick and there is no difference between copper and earthenware — Magen Avraham. Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote R' Yitzchak the White would not allow kneading in water that was in a copper vessel that heats the water — there was an incident and other rabbis forbade likewise. However, practice is to knead in copper vessels, as in Knesset HaGedolah and Kaf HaChayim s.k. 10. Or Zaru'a wrote an incident came before my elders, may they rest in Eden: one placed mayim matzah in a warm winter room; he asked if the vessel was hot when they took from it; he said no — and permitted.
baer-heitev/3:ב: Lukewarm. That is, like the warmth of saliva; and it is explained in Tur and Beit Yosef that in benefit it is permitted for everyone even if one kneaded with hot water.
baer-heitev/3:ג: B'shogeg. And he has no other dough — Magen Avraham. Taz wrote on the first night one may rely so as not to nullify the positive mitzvah of eating matzah, but not other days — rather he eats other things. (And Kaf HaChayim implies the opposite for matzah of the mitzvah in any case one should not take it — see there.)
baer-heitev/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two, Beit Yosef; but Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote it is nullified in the majority, and so too in Yoreh De'ah siman 98, Magen Avraham; and it is implied from the words of the poskim that if it became mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically that it became mixed before kneading. (And Kaf HaChayim ruled in the name of his brother-in-law the Gaon, may he rest in Eden, that he permitted even at the time of kneading.) And Ateret Zekenim raised that b'dieved one may permit even in such a case. And Magen Avraham wrote it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not because of prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so, it is permitted to cool them l'chatchila — requires study. And Kaf HaChayim wrote the same applies to copper-kettle water — this cooling helps according to all — and so too Ateret Zekenim.
baer-heitev/5:א: Salt. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape the faces of the matzah in salt water and return them to the oven as on chol ha'moed. And specifically on chol ha'moed scraping is permitted, but on the first two nights it is forbidden — see Taz.
baer-heitev/5:ב: To forbid. That is, in eating; but in benefit it is certainly permitted. And if he put a little salt in it, if it is baked immediately it is permitted in eating, for a little salt does not heat it entirely — Magen Avraham. And all this if one kneaded with water; but if one kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
baer-heitev/6:א: With caraway. Kimmel in Ashkenaz language.
baer-heitev/6:ב: Matzah. And in Rambam it implies it is rich matzah. And for everyone one must eat a kezayit of matzah aside from spices. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes the entire dough chametz; and the same applies to a little lime — Darkei Moshe. It appears specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted. It appears ginger is treated like pepper, and possibly the same for anise and saffron. Magen Avraham and Ateret Zekenim ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices except pepper. And even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as written in s.k. 15; and so Bach, Ateret Zekenim, and Kaf HaChayim. Dough kneaded in wine into which beer became mixed — Hagahot Beit Yosef wrote that since there is no water there is no need to be particular — Ateret Zekenim; see responsum Darkei Noam Orach Chayim siman 6 and Ginat Veradim general rule 4 siman 9.
baer-heitev/6:ד: Lime. This is live lime; but lime in a wall that already dried and hardened like stone — it appears plainly it does not forbid. Shevut Yaakov part 2 siman 13.
beer-hagolah/1:ג: Rashi and Ba'al HaHalachot Gedolot and most of the poskim
beer-hagolah/1:ה: Tur in the name of his father the Rosh
beer-hagolah/2:א: Orchot Chayim in the name of the Ra'avad
beer-hagolah/3:ד: Tur in the name of Mahariv and Maharitz Gaon — according to his explanation they disagree regarding water that was not left overnight; and likewise Rambam in chapter 5
beer-hagolah/3:ה: Tur according to Rashi's explanation, and likewise the Rosh there
beer-hagolah/4:_: Semag in the name of R' Yechiel and Semak
beer-hagolah/6:א: Rambam chapter 5, Rosh, and Mordechai end of chapter 3 of Pesachim — from that which is in Menachot 23
beer-hagolah/6:ב: Tur in the name of Rokeach; there 20; and pepper; and prohibition of spices — he wrote all of it in the name of the Ra'avad
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: A. A. A. A. A. A. A. A.D. is a woman who is not hanged but in our water:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And Rashi — we rule like R' Nachman there 94b: in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower sky; therefore the whole world is cold and springs boil. Rashi there: in the lower part of the sky, close to the ground, at the edges of the sphere; therefore the whole world is cold, for it travels only at the sides of the world; and springs boil — meaning near the water at the sides of the world from which springs come — end quote. Nissan is still considered rainy season. Therefore there is no difference between night and day — always in rainy season, day and night, it travels in the lower sky; only at night it travels in the vault of the sky and the sky separates between sun and earth, hence darkness on the earth; by day it travels in the hollow of the sky toward the earth, hence the earth is lit. Therefore no difference whether drawn by day or night — water is hot and needs 12 hours cooling; if drawn in the morning, permitted to knead with them in the evening after 12 hours. R' Yehuda uses mayim shelanu implying they draw in the evening and knead in the morning — common practice: people bake by day, therefore must leave all night and may bake immediately at dawn.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: And R' Eliezer of Metz — we rule like the admission of the sages of Israel to the sages of the nations there: no difference between summer and rainy season; always by day it travels below the sky (therefore it lights for us), and at night below the ground (therefore earth's thickness separates between sun and us, hence night darkens); therefore by day springs cold, at night boiling — at night the sun travels near the place springs issue; by day when the sun is far they cool. According to him, if drawn at bein ha shemashot, permitted to knead immediately, for they already cooled 12 hours attached by day. In this there is no dispute per R' Eliezer of Metz — only if drawn by day or night they disagree: R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi whether drawn day or night they have no remedy forever. Rabbeinu Yehuda challenged: if so why call them mayim shelanu? In any case if drawn at bein ha shemashot no overnight needed and permitted immediately; if drawn by day or night, overnight does not help — therefore Rabbeinu Yehuda: per R' Eliezer of Metz, if drawn by day they need overnight of the following night and it helps; if drawn at night they need the full night they were drawn and the day after and the night after. His reason and reasoning — see Beit Yosef who elaborated greatly. R' Yitzchak Saba's view is also like R' Eliezer of Metz here, for we rule like admission of sages of Israel; except where R' Eliezer of Metz holds if drawn at bein ha shemashot no overnight needed because they cooled 12 hours attached — R' Yitzchak Saba disagrees and requires 24 hours cooling; therefore draw at bein ha shemashot; then they cool 12 hours attached by day (for by day springs are cold) and need overnight all night and cool 12 hours detached (for at night the world is cold). Maharil leans like R' Yitzchak Saba. One should not be lenient to draw by day (meaning before close to bein ha shemashot, about half hour before) — per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct; meaning per R' Eliezer of Metz not correct per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi even if left all night, for they have no remedy; but per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ד: In this all agree. Meaning R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Rabbeinu Yehuda agree it is not correct per R' Eliezer of Metz to draw at night; they disagree: per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi they have no remedy forever; per Rabbeinu Yehuda overnight of the night drawn does not help; nevertheless overnight of the following night helps as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ה: And the water is forbidden to the world of the east
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: One may be lenient: first, one may rely on Rashi that 12 hours waiting suffices whether drawn by day or night as above; second, even R' Eliezer of Metz was stringent only l'chatchila when possible; when impossible, perhaps R' Eliyahu Mizrachi agrees to be lenient.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ז: Know Bach wrote further leniency per Raavan who holds for Rashi one does not need 12 hours at night but suffices until after dawn if the night was short. Authors ruled 12 hours for Rashi — fixed time by day if drawn in morning; in Nissan day and night are equal and night is 12 hours; therefore its measure by day equals places where in Nissan night is 12 hours — because we do not distinguish. But if drawn at evening bein ha shemashot, leaving the night as it is, even if short, permitted immediately at dawn — I copied his words to be a shield for people of the land who do not wait 12 hours and knead at dawn — they have whom to rely on; but most poskim did not write so and one should not be lenient. See siman 261 measure of bein ha shemashot; Magen Avraham wrote there it is about a quarter hour — see there; see here Taz s.v. regarding law, etc.; see Kaf HaChayim agreed with Magen Avraham that better to draw a little before bein ha shemashot than after — unlike Taz.
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (c) There is a quaint that will not fall as a quaint, and as a ‘lucky flame with another taste, but that will not fall is nothing but a substance’ in the midst of arrogance. But it means that when you walk the day under the air of the fire, you must cover them that they will not be warmed:
machatzit-hashekel/4:א: (s.k. 4) On the night of the 5th, etc. Explanation: for those who bake, etc. — meaning it is explained siman 458: when Pesach falls on Sunday one kneads Friday evening after chatzot; obviously one draws Thursday night. Rama needed to write this for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos, as Tur siman 458.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ב: Seeing the S.R. D.C., a slight preparation is not permitted by the High Court
machatzit-hashekel/4:ג: See siman 7 one may rely on Rabbeinu Yehuda — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ד: And b'dieved Bach is lenient if drawn at night. This is called b'dieved.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ה: See siman 307: shevut of shevut is permitted in a place of mitzvah; therefore permitted to command a gentile.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ו: And siman 464 — meaning although Rama wrote in this seif forbidden via gentile; he brought proof from siman 464 that kneading and baking are certainly forbidden via gentile, yet Magen Avraham wrote there when impossible otherwise permitted via gentile when Jew stands over — all the more so drawing. Or take water drawn in his house — meaning mayim shelanu even if not drawn for the mitzvah.
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: And so the rivers are cleared from the river, and therefore the rivers are boiled down from the river, and they are plucked out of the water when they continue to spring
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: But, etc. — always boiling; therefore wells are preferable.
magen-avraham/1:א: Close to bein ha shemashot. By right one should draw at bein ha shemashot itself so water cools 12 hours attached by day when springs are cold, and 12 hours in the air at night as Maharil wrote; but since impossible to measure bein ha shemashot precisely, permitted to draw close to bein ha shemashot. One should not be lenient to draw by day, for per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it is not correct — all the more so not to draw at night, for in this all agree. Beit Yosef wrote: if drawn after beginning of night they have no remedy and the water is forbidden forever per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — end quote Darkei Moshe; Bach wrote b'dieved if drawn at night one may be lenient to knead by day; see siman 261 measure of bein ha shemashot.
magen-avraham/1:ב: Not harmful. And even if they stood in the sun (Beit Yosef, Eliyah Rabbah); siman 459 seif 65.
magen-avraham/1:ג: They must be covered. Nothing will fall into the content, but it is not to be felt that it has already sunk
magen-avraham/1:ד: Thursday night. Explanation: for those who bake at Motzei Shabbos and cannot draw at Motzei Shabbos nor Friday when they need bein ha shemashot and Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov — therefore draw Thursday night belonging to Friday (Beit Yosef); see siman 467; if so, also those baking on second day of Yom Tov forbidden to draw at bein ha shemashot on Yom Tov, for one Yom Tov does not prepare for another and they need eve of 14th; see siman 458. It appears if he forgot Thursday night he may draw Friday while still day on this Erev Pesach, or command gentile at bein ha shemashot — see siman 307 and 464; or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for mitzvah since impossible otherwise.
magen-avraham/1:ה: From rivers. Because the sun travels in Nissan days under the ground and therefore wells boil; but melting of snow and rain always boils.
magen-avraham/1:ו: And not from wells. Because the sun travels under the ground.
magen-avraham/1:ז: One may not pour out. For "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil."
magen-avraham/1:ח: Or falling tekufah. And Yoreh De'ah siman 116 wrote there is danger only when drinking at the hour tekufah falls (and so Shulchan Aruch HaRav).
magen-avraham/1:ט: Iron. One does not put his hand in the water, for the hand heats — only hang on a cord (Maharil); rest of year salt or seal (Hagahot Maimoniyot, Darkei Moshe). Practice filters water (Maharil). Mateh Moshe: do not take vessel that had honey or fruit juice — fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz siman 462. (Boiling permitted — it appears.) Also not in copper vessel that heats — end quote; however I have seen kneading in copper troughs — Semag see there.
magen-avraham/1:י: Wooden vessel, etc. — the same for glazed earthenware; see siman 473 seif 3.
magen-avraham/2:_: Cistern. Building separates from ground and covered above — as if drawn.
magen-avraham/3:א: Large kettle. The copper of the kettle retains heat (Rashi); it does not deal with water heated on the fire, for then even if completely cooled it is forbidden even not in the kettle — merely putting water in the kettle without fire is forbidden because the kettle retains heat; so Agur in his responsum (Rama siman 35).
magen-avraham/3:ב: He was cut thick. His margin is thick and has not been divided between copper and debris on the Shabbat
magen-avraham/3:ג: In time of pressure. Bach explained: if no other water, permitted to knead; disagreed with Shulchan Aruch; it appears Shulchan Aruch did not intend to permit except if kneaded b'dieved and no other dough — Rama refers to this; wrote even without pressure permit if transgressed b'shogeg, etc. — see above seif 1.
magen-avraham/4:_: One in two. Implies less than that is not nullified (Beit Yosef); but Semag and Semak wrote nullified in majority, and so Yoreh De'ah siman 98; we rule see Ateret Zekenim; it appears permitted to mix them l'chatchila, for the reason is not prohibition but when not left overnight they are hot and when mixed they become cold; if so permitted to cool l'chatchila — requires study.
magen-avraham/5:_: One should forbid. Thus Darkei Moshe; per his words siman 462 even b'dieved forbid; Mordechai: eating salted matzah like eating chametz — end quote; it appears if a grain of salt fell in, if baked immediately permitted as siman 462; if because of heating, rely on all that little salt does not heat entire dough — b'dieved siman 91.
magen-avraham/6:א: Sarah. And who should eat as an exalted olive, except the spice, look at the landings of a page as a “g” in his daughter:
magen-avraham/6:ב: Since it has. Implies one fulfills with it on the first nights; however in Rambam it implies rich matzah; and so Maggid Mishneh chapter 6.
magen-avraham/6:ג: And pepper. Even one grain makes entire dough chametz; likewise a little lime (Darkei Moshe, Mahariv). It appears specifically kneaded into it; if fell on, remove and permitted. Ginger like pepper; possibly anise and saffron too. In hints it implies pepper permitted b'dieved; nevertheless do not be lenient — see above seif 65 regarding salt.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) One may not knead, etc. — whether matzah of the mitzvah or other matzot.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) Only with mayim shelanu — meaning overnight standing in a vessel after drawing. Rashi wrote in the Gemara: in Nissan days springs are hot because then the sun travels in the lower sky near earth and heats springs; some explain because at night the sun travels below the ground and heats springs; therefore sages forbade using them for kneading immediately upon taking from the ground [for they are like hot water forbidden for kneading as below seif 3] until they stand in vessels and cool from their heat; measure of standing in vessels and time of drawing from the well will be explained below.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) Whether river water — although not from springs and reasons above do not apply, nevertheless be stringent also to cool them because sun's heat by day warmed them somewhat.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) Close to bein ha shemashot — l'chatchila it is fitting and proper to draw at bein ha shemashot itself so water cools 12 hours attached by day when springs are cold and 12 hours in air at night; but since impossible to measure bein ha shemashot precisely, permitted to draw close to bein ha shemashot. One should not be lenient l'chatchila to draw much while still day — all the more so not after nightfall; nevertheless b'dieved if drawn much while still day one should not be stringent and may knead l'chatchila after overnight; see Biur Halacha. Likewise if drawn at night before chatzot, permitted to knead tomorrow l'chatchila, but must wait 12 hours from drawing.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (e) or between the suns - to move on the whole night water that will slip from the connected. And between the suns is after the sunset sinks up to the stars and the day It is better to get ahead of after:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (b) The entire night, and in the hour of the pressure, it should be easy for them to be saved after the dawn of the PLO that did not stand for hours:
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (c) We will fight in the basement that is cold – and if it does not have a cell that will be built inside the house and in a room that does not rule it:
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (8) For the cellar is warm — if placed in cellar or heated house it will be explained below in the gloss.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (9) Before sunrise — lest they heat from sun's heat; it deals when water stands outside where sun rises from there; if where he cannot see the sun's face, no concern — as siman 259 seif 1 — see there; however on cloudy day in every case must be careful to bring in before sunrise hour, for a cloudy day is entirely sun.
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (e) Until they were fought, and if they were to be criminalized, they would fight for blood and anemia in the SJ. Pushin was called when he was rocky and looked at the blanket he wrote that he had been warmed A little warmth that is not the warmth of the rock should not be borne in them:
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (a) It is not harmful – and even in the sun, all that have not been fought is permitted to be eaten in them:

turei-zahav/1:_: One may not knead, etc. Thus the Rosh: because in Nissan days the springs boil and it is still the rainy season and the sun travels in the lower sky — therefore one fills from evening and they cool until morning. R' Avigdor wrote: according to this reason, one who draws in the morning and leaves until evening is fine; but R' Eliyahu Mizrachi explained: because at night the sun travels under the earth, therefore they have no remedy except not to be attached at night; therefore those who draw at the beginning of the night are permitted immediately and forbidden to draw after the beginning of the night — end quote. Thus Semag: R' Eliezer of Metz says even l'chatchila one may knead with them when impossible, as said at the end of chapter Kol Sha'ah: Rav Matna expounded in Papunia — a woman should knead only in mayim shelanu; tomorrow they all brought their jugs to him, thinking shelanu meant Rav Matna's water; he told them: I mean water from my house — meaning they left overnight; and we do not find they fasted from eating. Rashi explained the reason for mayim shelanu: because the sun travels in Nissan days which is still rainy season, etc.; according to his reason, drawing in the morning and leaving until evening is permitted; and from Papunia there is no proof — but the reason must be because at night the sun travels under the ground; therefore one who draws at the beginning of the night is permitted immediately; therefore forbidden after drawing after the beginning of the night — end quote. Rambam and R' Yehuda bar Natan ruled in commentary on Pesachim: forbidden to bake before dawn; if they baked, the baked product should be forbidden lest the end of the night causes cooling — however this prohibition applies only to Rashi, not R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — end quote. R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote on what Semag wrote \"we do not find they fasted from eating\": it appears it was during Pesach when they kneaded in water not left overnight; when he said \"I mean from my house,\" he presumably permitted kneading in water not left overnight — you will ask: on that day they ate no matzah but fruits — why did the Talmud not mention this to teach us? One cannot say he permitted the baked matzot that were shogeg in kneading, for only \"if one transgressed and kneaded\" did Rav Ashi forbid, but shogeg not, and he would not permit l'chatchila, for presumably they destroyed all their matzot before coming to him because of chametz prohibition (and per this reasoning the Talmud need not mention shogeg is permitted); if it was the Shabbos before Pesach, what of \"we do not find they fasted\" — they already ate chametz four hours on the first night, and in the evening they could already knead with water drawn in the morning after 12 hours per Rashi, or draw at beginning of night permitted immediately per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, etc.; but the question is: whence that exposition was during Pesach — perhaps on Shabbos before Pesach, and he permitted on the first night for fulfillment of eating matzah, not during Pesach where there is no mitzvah fulfillment — end quote Mizrachi's words. Objection on him per his reasoning: he asked perhaps it was Shabbos before Pesach — why did he need to ask because of matzah fulfillment; he should have asked perhaps he expounded Shabbos before Pesach not to draw except mayim shelanu and they thought Rav Matna's water, and on the first night he said draw on the first night per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi who need not distinguish first night from rest of Pesach — forced distinction as Beit Yosef wrote on him: wherever chametz prohibition applies there is no distinction; or he should have asked from what he himself said to prove R' Eliyahu Mizrachi held the exposition was during Pesach not Shabbos before, and therefore asked whence for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi it was not Shabbos before — Beit Yosef already sensed this. It appears to me on the contrary R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds the exposition was Shabbos before, as all who want to learn Pesach laws before Pesach; what Mizrachi wrote they already ate chametz four hours on the first night — I wonder why Mizrachi did not analyze R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words \"we do not find they fasted from eating\" — why not say they fasted alone and this \"from eating\" is extra language; rather it appears not a full fast all day but on mealtime which is beginning of the night itself, for they hurry to eat lest children sleep, as siman 472; and he holds as Tur siman 458 in the name of R' Yehuda HaKohen: on Yom Tov night one should not trouble on Yom Tov to bake matzah — therefore it fits here: you will ask they drew beginning of Pesach night and delayed in drawing, kneading, arranging, baking — mealtime which is on the first night by law would be lost; therefore he said we do not find they fasted from eating — meaning the proper mealtime; rather certainly he permitted kneading immediately in water not left overnight. Granted for Rashi no proof — one could say they had other water at home and waited until after chatzot and baked matzah after 12 hours and ate in evening; but per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi there is proof as written; thus other difficulties of Mizrachi that Beit Yosef brought are settled. Mizrachi wrote further: per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi he must hold if drawn before beginning of night while sun still on earth, forbidden to knead, because they must be attached in earth by day when earth is cold and cools them — otherwise no proof from Papunia even per his words that we can say they left what was drawn by day; and from \"one who draws at beginning of night\" it implies if drawn before beginning or after, no — end quote. Beit Yosef disagrees: if so how does it say one may knead only in mayim shelanu — what is night's work: if drawn while sun on earth or after beginning of night, even ours forbidden; if at beginning of night, even not ours permitted; rather should have written one may knead only in what was drawn at bein ha shemashot; therefore he explained per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi three divisions: drawn at bein ha shemashot — permitted immediately; drawn after beginning of night — wait another day and night; drawn by day — wait that day and following night; and when he said mayim shelanu until they stood one full night and cooled in coldness — when drawn after beginning of night the reason is heat of sun under ground; when drawn by day, although earth is cold, they do not cool from boiling until 12 hours pass; and since the world is hot by day and water heats when drawn by movement as Rif and Ran wrote, they do not cool until one night; but drawn at bein ha shemashot, although they heat when drawn by movement, R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds since the world is cold then they cool immediately. Therefore \"one who draws at beginning of night permitted immediately\" means then permitted immediately; but if drawn before beginning while sun on earth or after beginning, forbidden until full night passes. And \"they have no remedy except not to be at night attached\" — not that no remedy forever, rather remedy of 12 hours detached does not help when drawn by day or after beginning of night, only one full night — end Beit Yosef; many questions on Rabbeinu Yehuda's explanation, for night's stringency is from one of two ways: either because in measure of night the boiling in them cools as Rashi, or at night itself there is boiling per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi; per Beit Yosef's words of R' Eliyahu Mizrachi when drawn by day they heated from movement and need one night to cool; when drawn at night they boil from the night per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — he should hold two powers in that night: cooling and fixing boiling drawn by day, and second boiling of water attached at night — why did R' Eliyahu Mizrachi write drawn at bein ha shemashot permitted immediately, whence — since anyway there is boiling from drawing movement, certainly here too needs full night to cool like by day. What Beit Yosef wrote: since bein ha shemashot is cold they cool immediately is very astonishing — whence for Rambam boiling cools in one moment as soon as they draw; and since day's boiling by movement and bein ha shemashot's boiling are equal, why does drawing by day not suffice to wait until bein ha shemashot and cool as drawn at bein ha shemashot; a fortiori drawing by day whose time is longer should help bein ha shemashot's cooling for day's drawing boiling, since bein ha shemashot's cooling helps what was drawn at bein ha shemashot when boilings are equal — I do not know place to settle our rabbi Beit Yosef's words and why he troubled to explain \"they have no remedy\" that R' Eliyahu Mizrachi mentioned and why he asked what does Semag bring proof from Papunia per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and not Rashi — granted for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi no proof, perhaps drawn at beginning of night; Beit Yosef explained Semag's proof: Gemara needed this incident of Papunia which is not for need — implying it teaches permission to knead in water not left overnight; granted for Rashi no proof — one could say it teaches leniency when drawn morning and wait until evening, unlike R' Eliyahu Mizrachi who is not satisfied with that — if so certainly Gemara wrote this incident to inform us water not left overnight is permitted when impossible — these are Beit Yosef's words though not his language. I wonder why the rabbi here deviated from his path of truth everywhere and inclined to sharp pepper and explained what did not occur to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi — he had proof from not finding they fasted from eating, and Rabbeinu Yehuda discarded that proof and wrote another proof: why Gemara needed this incident not mentioned in R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words; and per Beit Yosef's pilpul we too say for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi no proof — Gemara teaches mayim shelanu means water from his house — meaning night itself requires, not measure of overnight like Rashi where even by day helps; this certainly should be informed in Talmud; Mahari Weil also explained for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi overnight of night helps for drawn by day and washed his hands to explain Mizrachi who holds so; he raged at Beit Yosef who explained Mizrachi's words as mistaken — rather Mizrachi also holds so, except drawing at night he explains they have no remedy forever; astonishing, for Mizrachi explicitly wrote if drawn before beginning or after, no — clear before is like after with no distinction. And no reason ever to distinguish invalidity from day's boiling and night's boiling — who is the prophet to tell us there is distinction — Gemara did not mention this at all, only we require overnight without condition. It appears to me Mizrachi's explanation per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi is clear truth: for Rashi there is no boiling for night because it is night, but because rainy season and springs always boil day and night; night came only to fix boiling — cool at night time; thus also waiting by day measure of night suffices. R' Eliyahu Mizrachi holds night mentioned here is because there is boiling at night since sun travels under earth; by day obviously sun on earth and certainly boiling — Gemara teaches also at night there is boiling; night's boiling certainly not specifically when hot all night — if less than full night we do not say so — if so why insist overnight in detached, suffices part of night in detached; rather certainly also part of night has heat, at least most of night; this cannot be clarified — therefore sages required detached all night; not literally all night unless drawn at very beginning they had not yet received night's boiling in that moment — therefore R' Eliyahu Mizrachi permitted drawn at beginning of night implying literally at night but small measure. Tur wrote one who draws evening until sunset permitted immediately — comes to distance further from transgression, beware drawing even at beginning of night because of erring; it turns out Beit Yosef should have written one may knead only in water drawn at bein ha shemashot — truth is not so, for even drawn at beginning of night permitted, that too is called mayim shelanu; prohibition only in drawn large part of night; by day obvious to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi forbidden, not for reason Mizrachi said R' Eliyahu Mizrachi requires all day cold from earth's cold — one can answer when drawn by day placed in cellar or cave they cool too as Beit Yosef wrote; and if heat by day what does earth's cold help — only wonder; rather main point: heat by day sun on earth heats water; at night sun under earth heats; no permission except hour without heat — beginning of night, and all the more bein ha shemashot before it; all forbidden drawn in hour of boiling day or after beginning of night have no remedy — like hot water cooling never helps; all this R' Eliyahu Mizrachi learned from Talmud \"one may knead only in mayim shelanu\" — had it said by day permitted, should have said only drawn by day; had it said part of night forbidden at beginning, should have said only drawn at bein ha shemashot or one may not knead water drawn at night except certainly also at night there is permission — beginning; therefore said shelanu meaning like way of overnight called see most of night called overnight for person too; we learn if drawn at beginning of night properly called mayim shelanu; R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Semag words are correct and clear: R' Eliyahu Mizrachi said proof l'chatchila permit water not left overnight when impossible — otherwise what did Papunia do after learning prohibition to eat evening at matzah mealtime — beginning of night immediately when needed to draw, knead, bake — not worth hiding; Talmud owner should inform they pushed mitzvah time for this — rather certainly permitted even l'chatchila when needed; Semag words on R' Yehuda bar Natan forbidden bake before dawn lest end of night causes cooling — on this: nevertheless this prohibition only Rashi — from tying night to cooling implies R' Yehuda bar Natan has other explanation in Rashi's words: boiling because rainy season and springs boil, need cooling, cooling not time-dependent but specifically at night when cold; also at night itself perhaps specifically end of night causes cooling when north wind blows as Semak — therefore Semag wrote nevertheless this prohibition only Rashi — \"nevertheless\" implies R' Yehuda bar Natan does not hold like Rashi that Semag brought first that 12 hours depends, rather specifically at night from night's cooling they become permitted; but for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi this prohibition does not apply — end of night for cooling — for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi we do not tie cooling to night, night used only for prohibition; if drawn after beginning forbidden forever; if at beginning no prohibition — why need dawn; we are raised to settle Rabbeinu Yehuda's difficulty on Mizrachi in Hagahot Maimoniyot ch. 1 R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words and \"some forbid\" when drawn while still day even if left all night afterward — Mizrachi's view is R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's view; what \"some forbid\" — I wonder, for Beit Yosef rejected that view as his proof that forbidden even with overnight when drawn while still day; behold we explicitly find this view \"some forbid\"; why not attribute also to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi; Gemara's \"some forbid\" is no contradiction to Mizrachi, for R' Eliyahu Mizrachi did not explicitly forbid while still day as \"some forbid\"; find Tur siman 461 after Rabbenu Tam wrote \"some forbid\" — Rabbenu Tam himself just did not mention in explanation; our words in Semak siman 291: one may knead only in mayim shelanu; some stringent to draw water between day and night; Rabbi R' Yitzchak says Torah was not given to ministering angels; further should have taught shelanu all night — rather overnight only from midnight until dawn when north wind blows — end quote; explained as above: \"some forbid\" is R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's view — permitted at beginning of night, stringent not to draw even at beginning, only between day and night; R' Yitzchak says since by law permitted at beginning and we are not angels to measure precisely when begins, certainly by law from midnight until dawn. For law Beit Yosef ruled draw while still day or bein ha shemashot and do not knead until their entire night passes — \"while still day\" is his view explaining R' Eliyahu Mizrachi: drawn by day has remedy next night; per Mizrachi drawn by day or after beginning of night no remedy forever — this explanation is absolute truth as written; therefore do not practice drawing while still day although not forbidden to draw while still day and leave afterward — one may rely on Rashi; nevertheless l'chatchila avoid until sunset; delaying somewhat profits more, for even at beginning of night full permission as written; whoever doubts sunset should delay and not advance — and so Mordechai end chapter Kol Sha'ah: ancestors drew after sunset; Behag wrote mitzvah to fill water between suns and stars — end quote; so practice halacha l'maaseh.
turei-zahav/2:_: L'chatchila one should draw, etc. Rashi wrote main stringency of water not left overnight is in springs and cisterns that boil, but not rivers — in Nissan sun does not travel in water, but sages were concerned for most towns that have only cistern and spring water; R' Avigdor wrote this is nothing, for even flowing rivers sun strikes by day and heats them; therefore better l'chatchila to draw from river when possible.
turei-zahav/3:_: One should not discard, etc. Reason in Mordechai: night of guarding is for Thursday; also wrote even other Pesach nights "He guards the simple" — heaven forbid mishap in mitzvah matzot — end quote; nevertheless appears other nights he may discard if easily without those waters, unlike night before Pesach which are for matzah of mitzvah — forbidden to discard, contemptuous of mitzvah, showing he holds mitzvah does not protect from mishap and verse "keeper of mitzvah knows no evil" is light in his eyes.
turei-zahav/4:_: Iron. One should be careful with the iron placed in the water to place it in a manner that he will not need to put his hand in at the time of kneading, for his hand heats the water; also the iron should be clean (so too Maharil):
turei-zahav/5:_: Cistern. Room built beneath and around — they are as collected in a vessel and do not boil from sun traveling under ground, for building separates from ground; but Beit Yosef reported: these waters in winter are hot like well water; therefore do not be lenient unless pressure — meaning close to drawing.
turei-zahav/6:_: Even without pressure, etc. R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, Semag, and Semak permit even l'chatchila when impossible otherwise; appears first night one may rely so as not to nullify eating matzah mitzvah since b'shogeg permitted; not other days — eat other things. Beit Yosef brought Mordechai: incident Pesach Sunday, tekufah fell Thursday night before; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night; R' Yehuda HaChasid wrote no concern — keeper of mitzvah; Mordechai after: baked only for day 1, Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow; Rokeach brought this law but there writes tekufa fell Thursday night only. It appears he understood tekufa fell Shabbos night, drew at night, baked Motzei matzah — night 1 Pesach; thus Mordechai explained; they did not want draw Motzei night per Rashi requiring 12 hours always, not concerned tekufa at drawing hour; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done keeper of mitzvah — implies bake Pesach night when Sunday; otherwise only Motzei bake no place for Mordechai; Beit Yosef further even so Mordechai not settled — wonder why crossed tekufa danger, not draw Friday day; answered perhaps hold by day no remedy per R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Mizrachi — Beit Yosef; perhaps hold such not mayim shelanu — Mizrachi; Bach asked why concerned Shabbos drawing tekufa — implies without tekufa no doubt; even without, Shabbos drawing prohibition; you will say such permitted Shabbos — then how draw afterward at night; why concerned tekufa at all since not at kneading hour; answered hold all water detached at tekufah hour dangerous even after — not answering other questions to explain Beit Yosef per his understanding. Mahari Weil other explanation per Beit Yosef — I did not reconcile; truth in Mordechai unlike Beit Yosef: drew Motzei Friday night only after drawing that night or Shabbos night tekufa — no difference; why Mordechai wrote Thursday night not Thursday 6: drew as law Motzei Friday bein ha shemashot, baked Yom Tov night — teaches two laws: tekufah does not harm what they kneaded for mitzvah though passed in detached; second that night baked only for Yom Tov 1 — two laws independent, both occurred — therefore Mordechai wrote also fell, etc., another novelty there; Shabbos obviously no drawing as Rokeach like filling garden end Eruvin — all Bach's questions inapplicable — in my humble opinion.
